CweFindings.Name: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type
CweFindings.Description: The product allows the upload or transfer of dangerous file types that are automatically processed within its environment.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync trusts the supplied Content-Type, retains the client filename extension, and accepts files even when Image.LoadAsync fails. An anonymous uploader can submit HTML with image/png and an .html extension. Original bytes are saved under wwwroot/uploads and served as HTML by static-file middleware, enabling same-origin stored script execution.

CweFindings.Name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CweFindings.Description: The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users.
CweFindings.Explanation: PhotoService.UploadPhotoAsync permits HTML bytes with an .html extension when Content-Type is image/png and image decoding fails. Static-file middleware serves these uploaded bytes as active HTML under the application origin. A victim following the public upload URL executes attacker-controlled script. This is the same root cause as CWE-434.
